stem:
Vihaan stirs a spoon of sugar into a glass of water. In another glass he stirs the same amount of sand into water.

Which claims are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Sugar mixes into the water to make a solution; the sugar particles are no longer seen as separate grains.
Sand does not dissolve; grains stay separate and can settle.
Sand dissolves just as sugar does because both were stirred into water.
Every solid added to water dissolves, so sand must dissolve just as sugar does.

teacher.key_rationale: Sugar dissolves to form a solution; sand does not dissolve and remains as separate grains. Treating stirred sand as dissolved, or expanding dissolve to every solid in water, misses the hinge.
